```{julia}
#| include: false

source = "test.qmd"

using EpidemicsCFTP, EpidemicsUtilities

using Gadfly, Compose
using DataFrames, PrettyTables

import Markdown

import Random
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

```{julia}
#| include: false
theme = create_theme(load_theme("config/test-theme.yml"))

set_default_plot_size(theme.figwidth, theme.figheight)
```

Construction of epidemics
=========================
Parameters: initial state and duration
--------------------------------------
We shall only use artificial examples, so there is no need to define rate parameters.
```{julia}
const duration = 5.0 ; const initial  = SIR(0.0, 4, 1, 0) ;
```

Construction of unconditioned epidemic
--------------------------------------
We work with an `Innovation`, used to generate an `Evolution` for an unconditioned epidemic.
Here are tables of the fields of `Innovation` and `Evolution`
(in each case only the first four fields are specified on creation: remaining fields
are computed
from input data):

::: {layout-ncol=2}

```{julia}
#| echo: false
pretty_table(DataFrame(name=[fieldnames(Innovation)...], type=[fieldtypes(Innovation)...]),
    header=(["Innovation", ""], ["field", "Type"]), alignment=[:l, :r])
```


```{julia}
#| echo: false
pretty_table(DataFrame(name=[fieldnames(Evolution)...], type=[fieldtypes(Evolution)...]),
    header=(["Evolution", ""], ["field", "Type"]), alignment=[:l, :r])
```

:::


Useful abbreviations for some imports from `EpidemicsCFTP`:
```{julia}
#| echo: false
labels   = [:AI  :AIF :I  :P  :R  :C]
import EpidemicsCFTP: AI, AIF, I, P, R, C
pretty_table(map(eval, labels), header=vec(labels), alignment = :l)
```


We construct an `Innovation` and a corresponding `Evolution` as follows.
```{julia}
uiv1 = Innovation(initial.n, 
    I[I(2t-1, t, t+1) for t ∈ [1,2]] ∪ AIF[I(0,3,4), I(2,4,5)], 
    [R(2t, t) for t ∈ [1,2]] ∪ [R(1,5), R(3,5), R(4,5)])
```
The corresponding `Evolution` of an (_unconditioned_) epidemic is given as follows:
```{julia}
uev1 = Evolution(initial, uiv1)
```

Construction of conditioned epidemic
------------------------------------
A `CEvolution` is a variant of `Evolution` with conditioned removals (`CRemoval`s),
with further computed fields filled if generated by a previous `AbstractEvolution`
with a candidate `Innovation`.
```{julia}
#| echo: false
pretty_table(DataFrame(name=[fieldnames(CEvolution)...], type=[fieldtypes(CEvolution)...]),
    header=(["CEvolution", ""], ["field", "Type"]), alignment=[:l, :r])
```
Again in the standard invocation
only the first four fields are specified on creation: other fields are computed
from the input data.

Here is a `Innovation` to generate the `CEvolution` of the corresponding conditioned epidemic:
```{julia}
iv1 = Innovation(initial.n, uev1.infections, 
        R[z for z ∈ setdiff(uev1.removals, uev1.history)], 
        C[C(z) for z ∈ uev1.removals ∩ uev1.history])
```
Here is the resulting `CEvolution` of an epidemic (_conditioned_ on observed removals) is:
```{julia}
ev1 = CEvolution(initial, iv1)
```
Notice that the fields `LFE`, `NFZ1`, `NFZ2`, `NFZ` of this `CEvolution` 
are in fact empty lists.
This particular `CEvolution` then corresponds to the state of the epidemic at step `0` of algorithmic time.
Thus there is no `AbstractEvolution` acting as predecessor in the sense of algorithmic time,
to provide information to compute these fields.

{{< pagebreak >}}

Tabular and graphical displays of epidemics
===========================================
`EpidemicsUtilities` supplies some constants 
used for the plotting parameter `select`, namely
```{julia}
import EpidemicsUtilities: ACTIVATED, REGIONS, BOUNDARIES, BASIC, ELEMENTS, LFE, LFET, LFER, MOST, NFZ
```

Here is a table of the evolution of the epidemic

```{julia}
#| echo: false 
uflow = table_trajectories1(duration, uev1.trajectory) ;
header = [:t, :susceptibles, :infectives, :removals, :epidemic]
Markdown.parse(pretty_table(String, uflow[:,header], 
  header=header, tf=tf_markdown, alignment=[:l, :c, :c, :c, :c]))
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
axes_plot = plot(uflow, yintercept=1:initial.n,
    Geom.hline(style=:dash, size=0.1mm, color=theme.scaffold),
    Coord.cartesian(xmin=0, xmax=duration, ymin=0, ymax=initial.n + 0.25),
    Guide.xlabel("Process time", orientation=:horizontal),
    style(default_color=theme.background),
    Theme(
        panel_fill=theme.blank,
        default_color=theme.default,
        background_color=theme.background,
        major_label_font="CMU Serif",   minor_label_font="CMU Serif",
        minor_label_color=theme.legend, major_label_color=theme.legend,
        major_label_font_size=8pt,     minor_label_font_size=6pt,
        grid_line_width=0mm,
)) ;

push!(axes_plot, layer(uflow, x=:t, y=:empty, Geom.line,
    style(line_width=2theme.trail, default_color=theme.scaffold))) ;

lines_plot = new_figure(axes_plot,
    Scale.y_continuous(labels=(initial.n ≤ EpidemicsUtilities.MAXPOP ?
        i -> EpidemicsUtilities.timelinelabels_circled(i; n=initial.n) :
        i -> EpidemicsUtilities.timelinelabels_bracketed(i; n=initial.n))),
    Guide.yticks(ticks=collect(1:(initial.n))),
    Guide.ylabel("Time lines")) ;

depict("test-01-unconditioned", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), uev1, duration, theme=theme, select=MOST),
        title="Evolution of unconditioned epidemic")
) ;

depict("test-01-conditioned", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), ev1, duration, theme=theme, select=MOST),
        title="Evolution of conditioned epidemic")
) ;
```

@fig-test-01-unconditioned and @fig-test-01-conditioned respectively 
plot incidents and evolutions of the unconditioned and conditioned epidemics.

::: {#fig-test-01-pair layout-ncol=2}

![Unconditioned epidemic `uev1`.](image/test-01-unconditioned.pdf){#fig-test-01-unconditioned}

![Conditioned epidemic `ev1`.](image/test-01-conditioned.pdf){#fig-test-01-conditioned}

Unconditioned (`uev1`) and conditioned (`ev1`) evolutions of epidemic.  Note that the only difference is that 
the two activated removals become `CRemoval`s. (Creation of a `CEvolution` `ev1` raises an error
if activated removals for `ev1` are not precisely the `CRemoval`s!)

:::

{{< pagebreak >}}




Taking a single step in algorithmic time
========================================

We introduce a new ("candidate")
`Innovation`, which will be used (indirectly) to derive a single step in algorithmic time
of the entire `CEvolution` trajectory.
```{julia} 
iv2c = Innovation(initial.n, 
    AIF[I(0.75,1,2), I(1.5,1,2), I(0.8,3,4), I(1.5,2,3), I(2.5,1,2), I(3.3,3,4), 
        I(3.6,4,5), I(3.9,4,5), I(4.5,1,3), I(4.4,3,4)], 
    R[R(0.5,2), R(2,3), R(1.2,4), R(3.3,1), R(4.5,5), R(4.8,1)], 
    C[C(2, 2), C(4,5)])
```
@fig-test-02-candidate and @fig-test-02-conditioned respectively plot the candidate innovation for step \(2\)
(@fig-test-02-candidate) and a repeat 
from @fig-test-01-conditioned
of the conditional epidemic evolution at step \(1\) (@fig-test-02-conditioned).
```{julia}
#| echo: false
depict("test-02-candidate", new_figure(
    draw_innovation!(deepcopy(lines_plot), iv2c, theme=theme, select=ELEMENTS),
        title="Candidate innovation")
) ;
```


::: {#fig-test-02-innov layout-ncol=2}

![Candidate innovation `iv2c` for step 2.](image/test-02-candidate.pdf){#fig-test-02-candidate}

![Conditioned evolution `ev1` of step 1.](image/test-01-conditioned.pdf){#fig-test-02-conditioned}


Candidate innovation `iv2c` and previous evolution `ev1` of epidemic.
@fig-test-02-conditioned repeats @fig-test-01-conditioned, to aid comparison between the candidate innovation
`iv2c`
and the conditioned evolution 
`ev1`
of one step previous in algorithmic time.
Direct generation of a `CEvolution` from a candidate innovation typically fails to respect removal-conditioning, so raising an error.


:::



{{< pagebreak >}}

Construction of the next algorithmic step
-----------------------------------------
We compute step `2` of the evolution of the conditioned epidemic in algorithmic time, using
the candidate `Innovation`
`iv2c` to generate the new conditioned evolution (`CEvolution`) `ev2`.
```{julia}
ev2  = CEvolution(ev1, iv2c)
```


{{< pagebreak >}}

Substitution of appropriate inactivated removals
------------------------------------------------
The first step is to create `iv1_2`, an intermediate `Innovation` which 

(a) removes _all_ old unconditioned
`Removal`s (@fig-test-03-removals1) (generating `iv1_1`) and 
(b) inserts those new `Removal`s which remain inactivated (@fig-test-03-removals2).
```{julia}
iv1_1 = Innovation(initial.n, ev1.infections, R[], ev1.cremovals)
ev1_1 = CEvolution(initial, iv1_1)
iv1_2 = Innovation(initial.n, ev1.infections, 
    EpidemicsCFTP.inactive_removals(ev1, iv2c), ev1.cremovals)
ev1_2 = CEvolution(initial, iv1_2)
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
depict("test-03-removals1", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), ev1_1, duration, theme=theme, select=MOST),
        title="Old removals removed")
) ;
depict("test-03-removals2", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), ev1_2, duration, theme=theme, select=MOST),
        title="New inactive removals inserted")
) ;
```


::: {#fig-test-03-removals layout-ncol=2}

![Conditioned evolution `ev1_1`.](image/test-03-removals1.pdf){#fig-test-03-removals1}

![Conditioned evolution `ev1_2`.](image/test-03-removals2.pdf){#fig-test-03-removals2}

Modifying inactivated removal structure.
_All_ unconditioned old `Removal`s are removed in @fig-test-03-removals1:
@fig-test-03-removals2 inserts only those new `Removal`s _not_ activated by the old evolution.

:::


Modifying conditional removal structure
---------------------------------------

The next step is to substitute only (the marks of) those `CRemoval`s which then remain activated, while continuing
to use the old `Infection`s
(@fig-test-04-cremovals1, @fig-test-04-cremovals2  depict resulting `Innovation`, `CEvolution`).
```{julia}
iv1_3 = Innovation(initial.n, ev1.infections, ev1_2.removals, 
    EpidemicsCFTP.resulting_cremovals(ev1, iv2c))
ev1_3 = CEvolution(initial, iv1_3)
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
depict("test-04-cremovals1", new_figure(
    draw_innovation!(deepcopy(lines_plot), iv1_3, theme=theme, select=ELEMENTS),
        title="Innovation up to new CRemovals")
) ;
depict("test-04-cremovals2", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), ev1_3, duration, theme=theme, select=MOST),
        title="Resulting evolution")
) ;
```

::: {#fig-test-04-cremovals layout-ncol=2}

![`Innovation` with modified removals `iv1_3`.](image/test-04-cremovals1.pdf){#fig-test-04-cremovals1}

![Resulting conditioned evolution `ev1_3`.](image/test-04-cremovals2.pdf){#fig-test-04-cremovals2}

Modifying conditional removal structure. `CRemoval` marks (but not times) altered only when 
they still lead to activation of the relevant `CRemoval`.

:::

{{< pagebreak >}}


Adding infections from the \LFE
-------------------------------
```{julia}
#| echo: false
if EpidemicsCFTP.is_correct_LFE(ev2)
    Markdown.parse("""
To determine how to replace infections, 
we could apply `EpidemicsCFTP.last_feasible_evolution` to `ev1_3`
(in fact the resulting `ev1_4` yields the final `ev2.LFE`!).
The construction of `ev1_4.LFE=ev2.LFE` in @fig-test-05-LFE has been checked using `EpidemicsCFTP.is_correct_LFE` and is **valid**.
""")
else
    Markdown.parse("""
To determine how to replace infections, 
we could apply `EpidemicsCFTP.last_feasible_evolution` to `ev1_3`
(in fact the resulting `ev1_4`  yields the final `ev2.LFE`!),
According to `EpidemicsCFTP.is_correct_LFE`, the construction of `ev1_4.LFE` is **not** valid.
""")
end
```

```{julia}
last_feasible_new_infections = AIF[z for z ∈ ev2.LFE ∩ iv2c.infections]
perpetuated_infections       = P[PInfection(z) for z ∈ ev2.LFE ∩ ev1_3.infections]
other_older_infections       = setdiff(ev1_3.infections, AIF[z for z ∈ ev2.LFE if z isa AIF])
iv1_4 = Innovation(initial.n, perpetuated_infections ∪ last_feasible_new_infections ∪ 
                        other_older_infections, ev1_3.removals, ev1_3.cremovals)
ev1_4 = CEvolution(initial, iv1_4, LFE=ev2.LFE)
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
depict("test-05-LFE1", new_figure(
    draw_innovation!(deepcopy(lines_plot), iv1_4, theme=theme, select=ELEMENTS),
        title="`Innovation` with LFE infections")
) ;
depict("test-05-LFE2", new_figure(
    draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), ev1_4, duration, theme=theme, select=MOST | LFE),
        title="Evolution with LFE infections")
) ;
```


::: {#fig-test-05-LFE layout-ncol=2}

![`Innovation` with LFE infections added (`iv1_4`).](image/test-05-LFE1.pdf){#fig-test-05-LFE1}

![Resulting conditioned evolution `ev1_4`.](image/test-05-LFE2.pdf){#fig-test-05-LFE2}

This adds \LFE (LFE) infections, calculated using `iv2c`, also highlighting
the region lying between the
LFE trajectory and the removal boundary.
Note perpetuation of the activated infection from time line 2 to time line 3,
carried over from `ev1_3`.

:::

Examples of progress through algorithmic time
=============================================

Extremal conditional evolutions
-------------------------------
We now demonstrate how this construction leads to progressive development through algorithmic time,
using `EpidemicsCFTP.is_correct_LFE` and `EpidemicsCFTP.is_correct_NFZ` to verify each step.
We seed the random number generator so as to ensure repeatability.
```{julia}
Random.seed!(2) ;
```

Initial `CEvolution`s can be _maximal_ or _minimal_; their definitions depend on
the times of the `CRemoval`s, which are supplied as a vector of times. 
Both require an `initial` state (of which only the fields `t` and `n` matter),
`duration`,
and a list of `CRemoval` times.

Initial computations of minimal and maximal `CEvolution`s
are illustrated in @fig-test-08-initial.
```{julia}
ev0_min = extremal_evolution(initial, duration, [z.t for z ∈ iv1.cremovals]; maximal=false) ;
ev0_max = extremal_evolution(initial, duration, [z.t for z ∈ iv1.cremovals]) ;
```

```{julia}                   
#| echo: false                       
SELECTION = ELEMENTS | BOUNDARIES | ACTIVATED

depict("test-08-minimal", new_figure(                                                  
   draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), ev0_min, duration, theme=theme, select=SELECTION),
         title="Minimal initial evolution")                                                     
) ; 
depict("test-08-maximal", new_figure(                                                  
   draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), ev0_max, duration, theme=theme, select=SELECTION),
         title="Maximal initial evolution")                                                     
) ; 
```


::: {#fig-test-08-initial layout-ncol=2}

![Minimal conditioned evolution.](image/test-08-minimal.pdf){#fig-test-08-minimal}

![Maximal conditioned evolution.](image/test-08-maximal.pdf){#fig-test-08-maximal}

Comparative trajectories of maximal and minimal conditioned evolutions.

:::

{{< pagebreak >}}

Progress starting with minimal (slowest) evolution
--------------------------------------------------
We generate a short sequence of candidate innovations, starting with the minimal evolution,
and use these to generate successive `CEvolution`s up to algorithmic time `ALG`.
We use the expressive "diamond" infix operator `⋄`, as in `ev = ev ⋄ iv`, instead of `ev = CEvolution(ev, iv)`.
Note that exceptions will be raised if `LFE` or `NFZ` structures appear to be wrong.
See the image sequence in @fig-test-09-minstep.
```{julia}
ALG=12 ; α=0.2 ; β=0.1
iv_null  = Innovation(initial.n, I[], R[], ev0_min.cremovals; duration=duration, α=α, β=β)
iv_seq   = [rand(iv_null) for i ∈ 1:ALG] ;
```

```{julia}
ev, minimal = ev0_min, CEvolution[]
for iv ∈ iv_seq[1:ALG]
    ev = ev ⋄ iv
    EpidemicsCFTP.is_correct_LFE(ev)
    EpidemicsCFTP.is_correct_NFZ(ev)
    push!(minimal, ev)
end ;
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
for (i, ev) ∈ enumerate(minimal[1:6])
    depict("test-09-minstep$i", new_figure(
        draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), ev, duration, theme=theme,
                select=BOUNDARIES | ELEMENTS | ACTIVATED | LFET| NFZ),
            title="Min evolution, step $i")
        ) ;
end
```


Progress starting with maximal (fastest) evolution
--------------------------------------------------
We now use this to generate successive `CEvolution`s
in algorithmic time but starting from maximal `CEvolution`.
See the image sequence in
@fig-test-10-maxstep.
```{julia}
ev, maximal = ev0_max, CEvolution[]
for iv ∈ iv_seq  
    ev = ev ⋄ iv
    EpidemicsCFTP.is_correct_LFE(ev)
    EpidemicsCFTP.is_correct_NFZ(ev)
    push!(maximal, ev)
end ;
```


```{julia}
#| echo: false
for (i, ev) ∈ enumerate(maximal[1:6])
    depict("test-10-maxstep$i", new_figure(
        draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), ev, duration, theme=theme,
                select=BOUNDARIES | ELEMENTS | ACTIVATED | LFET | NFZ),
            title="Max evolution, step $i")
        ) ;
end
```

Comparison of minimal and maximal sequences
-------------------------------------------
At this point we need to specify explicit colours.
```{julia}
using Colors
```
```{julia}
#| echo: false
plot_range = 1:6
Markdown.parse("""
Finally, @fig-test-11step plots the first 
$(plot_range[end])
steps of both minimal and maximal evolutions in algorithmic time. 
Monotonicity is 
$(all((minimal .≃ maximal)[findfirst(minimal .≃ maximal):end]) ? "maintained throughout" : "**not** maintained"),
while full coalescence (including agreement of `CRemoval` `target` fields) occurs at step $(findfirst(minimal .≃ maximal)) 
$(all((minimal .≃ maximal)[findfirst(minimal .≃ maximal):end]) ? "and then persists" : "but does **not** persist").
""")
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false   
for k ∈ plot_range
    work = draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), minimal[k], duration, theme=theme, 
                    select=BOUNDARIES, specified_color=colorant"red")                                                         
    depict("test-11step$k", new_figure(                                                  
        draw_evolution!(work, maximal[k], duration, theme=theme,
                    select=BOUNDARIES, specified_color=colorant"blue"),                                                          
            title="Evolution at step $k")                                                     
        )
end ;
```

Software versions
=================
Here is a table of software used in the following computations:
```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
quartoversion = "$(read(Cmd(`quarto --version`),          String)[1:end-1])"
ownversion    = "$(read(Cmd(`git describe --tags`),       String)[1:end-1])"
ownbranch     = "$(read(Cmd(`git branch --show-current`), String)[1:end-1])"
owndate       = replace(split(read(Cmd(`git log -1`), String), "\n")[3],
                        "Date:   " => "", " +0000" => "")

Markdown.parse("""
|_Software_                 |_Version_                      | _Branch_                     |_Date of last commit_       |
|:--------------------------|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------|:---------------------------|
|Quarto                     |`$(quartoversion)`             | ---                          |                            |
|Running under `julia`      |`$VERSION`                     | ---                          |                            |
|Module `EpidemicsCFTP`     |`$(EpidemicsCFTP.version)`     |`$(EpidemicsCFTP.branch)`     |`$(EpidemicsCFTP.date)`     |
|Module `EpidemicsUtilities`|`$(EpidemicsUtilities.version)`|`$(EpidemicsUtilities.branch)`|`$(EpidemicsUtilities.date)`|
|Quarto script `$(source)`  |`$(ownversion)`                |`$(ownbranch)`                |`$owndate`                  |
""")
```
